description: This dataset gives projected supply chain shocks caused by extreme weather events, measured as the annual percentage change in a country-sector's export activity compared with a 1990 to 2015 baseline. Values are annual from 2015 to 2099, global at country resolution, for SSP2 under RCP2.6 and RCP4.5 and five climate models (HadGEM2-ES, IPSL-CM5A-LR, GFDL-ESM2M, NorESM1-M and MIROC-ESM-CHEM), with rows keyed by scenario, climate model, country code and sector item. The method is econometric. It was produced by Stefan Borsky at the University of Graz in the EU Horizon 2020 COACCH project (co-designing the assessment of climate change costs) and deposited on Zenodo in 2021 as two downloadable CSV files, the data (about 20 MB) and a metadata sheet, under CC BY 4.0. Its recommended citation is COACCH deliverable D2.4 on impacts on industry, energy, services and trade. Caveats: shocks are statistical projections of trade exposure, not observed disruptions, the scenario set is limited to SSP2, and sector detail follows the trade classification, not infrastructure assets. It is useful for scenario inputs to supply chain resilience and capacity planning studies and for climate adaptation economics; a related record is the NGFS climate scenarios database.
